newsitem.title: USA: Biotech seen increasingly aimed at crop quality.
newsitem.headline: Biotech seen increasingly aimed at crop quality.

text.p: The genetic modification of crops in the United States is increasingly focused on improving product characteristics such as starch quality or oil content, a leading government scientist said.

John Payne, director of the U.S. Department of Agriculture Animal Plant Health Inspection Service's Biotechnology and Scientific Services, said herbicide tolerance had been the largest motivation during the last 10 years but product quality was "the segment which is growing most rapidly."

He said that in the period from 1987 to 1997 (up to January 31) herbicide tolerance had been the motivation behind 27.6 percent of genetic modifications, product quality 26.7 percent and insect resistance 24.3 percent.
Other factors included viral resistance (10.4 percent) and fungal resistance (3.8 percent).
Payne told USDA's annual agricultural outlook forum that the crops which had been most frequently modified were corn and tomatoes. Wheat was a recent addition to the list.
"It is fairly recently that the process has been developed for transforming wheat," he said.
